extracted.intended_audience: general readers; writers, comedians, and folklorists interested in joke/story forms
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive criteria for the comic subgenre 'shaggy-dog story' — long-winded anecdotes whose narration of irrelevant incidents culminates in an anticlimax or meaningless punchline. Useful to storytellers, comedians, and analysts who want to identify, write, or classify this type of joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extreme long-windedness / extensive narration of irrelevant incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: An extremely long-winded anecdote characterized by extensive narration of typically irrelevant incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The story length and the narration of many digressions or irrelevant details are central features; the tale may take several minutes (or much longer) to tell. The form exaggerates long-windedness as a comic device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination by an anticlimax
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The story's payoff is intentionally deflated: after a long buildup, the ending is trivial, disappointing, or otherwise subverts the expected payoff. This anticlimax is essential to the genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentionally silly or meaningless ending
rubrics_metrics.description: A long story that is intended to be amusing and that has an intentionally silly or meaningless ending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ending is often purposively pointless or absurd rather than a satisfying resolution; the point is the pointlessness itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derives humour from prolonged, purposeless setup (duration guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A lengthy shaggy-dog story derives its humour from the fact that the joke-teller held the attention of the listeners for a long time (such jokes can take five minutes or more to tell) for no reason at all, as the long-awaited resolution is essentially meaningless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration is a feature: part of the comic effect is that the audience invests time/attention expecting meaning. Practical note: many classic examples run five minutes or longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plays upon and subverts audience preconceptions of joke-telling
rubrics_metrics.description: Shaggy-dog stories play upon the audience's preconceptions of joke-telling. The audience listens to the story with certain expectations, which are either simply not met or met in some entirely unexpected manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective shaggy-dog stories deliberately manipulate expectations—setting up a conventional joke structure and then failing to deliver the anticipated comic payoff, or delivering it in a surprising, deflating way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humour lies in pointlessness or irrelevance of plot/punch line
rubrics_metrics.description: In such kind of humorous story, the humor lies in the pointlessness or irrelevance of the plot or punch line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or crafting a shaggy-dog story, assess whether the plot and punch line are rendered humorously irrelevant—the joke’s value comes from thwarting the search for meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archetypal structure: repeated emphasis culminating in trivial reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The archetype builds up a repeated emphasizing (e.g., the dog's exceptional shagginess) and culminates in a character reacting with a trivial dismissal (for example: 'That dog's not so shaggy').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A common structural device is repetition/accumulation of a motif followed by a minimal or dismissive final reaction that deflates the buildup. Variant archetypes exist (e.g., advertisement-and-butler endings) but the pattern of build-up + trivial negation is central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to unintentional long-windedness and deliberate construction
rubrics_metrics.description: As a comic device, the shaggy-dog story is related to unintentional long-windedness, and the two are sometimes both referred to in the same way; while a shaggy-dog story is a comic exaggeration of real-life experience, it is also deliberately constructed to play off an audience expecting a comic payoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between genuinely rambling anecdotes (unintentional) and deliberately crafted shaggy-dog jokes; both rely on length, but deliberate ones use that length strategically to subvert expectations.
